item.title: On the stability of displacement energy in toric manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.28469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a quantitative exploration of the behaviour of displacement energy of Lagrangians under stabilization. In particular, we completely characterize the displacement behaviour of toric fibres in Fano 4-manifolds. Our approach relates the geometry of the moment polytope's caustic to the structure of the (bulk-deformed) superpotential and to the presence of symmetric probes.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Philippe Chass\'e, Ipsita Datta

item.title: On the Maslov-type index for general paths of symplectic matrices
item.description: arXiv:2407.08433v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we define an index of Maslov type for general symplectic paths which have two arbitrary end points. This Maslov-type index is a partial generalization of the Conley-Zehnder-Long index in the sense that the degenerate set of symplectic matrices is larger. The method of constructing the index is direct without taking advantage of Maslov index of Lagrangian paths and consistent no matter whether the starting point of the path is identity or not, which is different from the ones for Long's Maslov-type index and Liu's $L_0$-index. Some natural properties for the index are verified. We review other versions of Maslov indices and compare them with our definition. In particular, this Maslov-type index can be regarded as a partial realization of Cappell-Lee-Miller index for a pair of Lagrangian paths from the point of view of index for symplectic paths.
item.dc:creator: Hai-Long Her, Qiyu Zhong

item.title: Quantization in polarization via transverse Poincar\'e-Birkhoff-Witt theorem
item.description: arXiv:2512.15060v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct, for every prequantizable symplectic manifold $(M,\omega,L)$ equipped with a nonsingular polarization, a deformation quantization $(C_M^\infty[[\hbar]],\star)$ together with a filtered sheaf of subalgebras $C_{M,\hbar}^{(<\infty)}$ that admits an exact action on polarized sections of $L^{\otimes k}$ for each $k\in\mathbb Z^+$. This extends the Kostant--Souriau action of polarization-preserving functions. The main geometric ingredient is a transverse PBW theory associated with a Nirenberg integrable distribution $P$. For any locally free $P$-modules $E$ and $E'$, we construct a PBW isomorphism for the bundle of transverse differential operators from $E$ to $E'$. This extends the PBW theorem for Lie pairs of Laurent-Gengoux--Sti\'enon--Xu to the setting of $P$-modules. After specializing $\hbar= \tfrac{\sqrt{-1}}{k}$, we obtain a sheaf $O_k^{(<\infty)}$ of level-$k$ quantizable functions and prove that its action identifies $O_k^{(<\infty)}$ with the sheaf of transverse differential operators on $L^{\otimes k}$. In the K\"ahler case, this recovers the construction of Chan--Leung--Li. Finally, for standard symplectic tori with real polarizations, we compare our construction with Toeplitz-type operators and obtain their semiclassical asymptotic expansions.
item.dc:creator: Dan Wang, Yutung Yau

item.title: Revisiting Gamma conjecture I: counterexamples and modifications
item.description: arXiv:2405.16979v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We continue investigation of asymptotics of quantum differential equation for Fano manifolds, with a special regard to Gamma conjecture I and its underlying Conjecture $\mathcal{O}$. We introduce the A-model conifold value, a symplectic invariant of a Fano manifold, and propose modifications for Gamma conjecture I based on this new definition. We discuss an interplay of birational transformations with an extension of Gamma conjecture I over the K\"ahler moduli space. These heuristics are applied to rigorously identify the principal asymptotic class in the case of $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundles $X_n=\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{P}^{n}}(\mathcal{O}\oplus\mathcal{O}(n))$. We observe, in particular, that for $X_n$ of dimension at least four, the Conjecture $\mathcal{O}$ holds just for even values of $n$, and in these cases we falsify the original non-modified Gamma conjecture I.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Galkin, Jianxun Hu, Hiroshi Iritani, Huazhong Ke, Changzheng Li, Zhitong Su

item.title: Non-degenerate mixed maps and contact structures
item.description: arXiv:2510.03033v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a theory of mixed isolated complete intersection singularities: real analytic maps $(\mathbb C^n,0)\to(\mathbb C^k,0)$ in the variables $z$ and $\bar z$ that are submersions along their punctured zero fiber. We give a Newton non-degeneracy criterion for this property and three sources of examples: Siegel maps arising from linear actions, mixed coverings, and mixed Hamm maps. For maps built from blocks of polar degree one that satisfy a weighted positivity condition, the punctured zero fiber is symplectic and every spherical link is contact, with the polar action as Reeb flow. Conversely, contact links of polar weighted maps force symplectic zero fibers, whereas the zero fibers of Siegel maps are coisotropic. Along the deformation of a mixed Hamm map to its holomorphic counterpart we prove exact symplectic rigidity: the punctured zero fibers are identified by equivariant maps that preserve the weighted Liouville form, the radius and every coordinate stratum. Hence all their links are strictly contactomorphic to the holomorphic Hamm link with its canonical contact structure, and the strict contact type depends only on the polar exponents and the dimensions. At each fixed radius these identifications extend to contact isotopies of the ambient weighted sphere. We also construct adapted open books, show that the ambient open books of mixed Hamm functions support the standard contact sphere, and deduce positive-stabilization equivalence in dimension three from Giroux's correspondence. Finally, we prove contact stability under higher-order perturbations of a radially homogeneous principal part.
item.dc:creator: In\'acio Rabelo, Jos\'e Seade

item.title: Finite-Rank Lie Algebroids for Singular Foliations of Prescribed Vanishing Order
item.description: arXiv:2608.07351v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a family of finite-rank Lie algebroids realizing, through their anchor maps, the singular foliations of vector fields vanishing to a prescribed order at the origin. The construction is obtained from the sub-adjacent Lie algebroids of a class of left-symmetric algebroids.
item.dc:creator: Austin Davis, Cheng-Yi Hung, Sangjun Ko, Kaichuan Qi

item.title: Non-planar contact structures with Calabi-Yau Fillings and topological quantum computation
item.description: arXiv:2610.25878v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper is a non-planar counterpart of the author's earlier work on planar contact structures and topological quantum computation. On a planar page every branch point is paired by a liftable arc, and the pairing matches the Ising representation exactly, in that fixing the channels of the pairs already fixes the state. Here the page has genus g and connected binding, presented as a simple degree-three cover of the disk. Every maximal system of disjoint liftable arcs then has exactly g members and leaves two branch points unused, and the half-twist interchanging the two points is not liftable, although its cube is and lifts to the identity. Ising fusion does not see that leftover pair, determining its channel from the other g and acting there only by scalars, whereas Fibonacci fusion can leave the channel undetermined. The powers of the cube then act by ten distinct relative phases on a single joint eigenspace, while the Calabi-Yau Stein filling stays fixed. An integral residue criterion supplies the Calabi-Yau test, a factorization localized on a contact connected sum is automatically Calabi-Yau, and, unlike in the planar case, a Calabi-Yau factorization need not be the shortest.
item.dc:creator: Atsuhide Mori
